text: Develop and calibrate a sound economic priority model
description: Maintain an inspectable, economically interpretable priority model that conserves graph value, attributes shared cost without duplication, discounts delayed returns, and presents a positive discounted-value/cost profitability ratio. Core mechanics now use strict positive real-idea costs, non-negative days-until-return, annual discounting, informational backward-compatible variance fields, SCC-condensed cyclic cost propagation, and a logarithmic break-even-centered color scale. Remaining work after acceptance is empirical calibration against authoritative observations from real deliveries: estimated versus actual duration, founder time, model/integration cost, external outcome, revenue, and prediction error. Do not auto-mutate human-set intrinsic value from activity counts or simulated credits.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Measured actual cost per idea gives the calibration the 30+ estimate/actual pairs it is waiting for within weeks instead of months.

status.comment: Economic priority refactor (18d9bbb) and the value-calculation rewrite (bb8150a8) are done. Calibration attempt 2026-11-02 with scripts/priority-calibration.mjs (actual effort = code churn of commits citing the idea): of 666 implemented ideas, 96% carry the default duration 1 and 84% the default cost 1; only 49 are cited by commits with code changes, 9 of those with a real cost estimate. Spearman(cost, churn) = 0.69 on those 9 (0.13 over all 49, diluted by defaults): promising but far too few. Waiting on data, not on a human: rerun the script when at least 30 estimated implemented ideas exist (create_idea now asks for a cost). Duration cannot be calibrated at all yet; nearly every idea keeps the default.
